## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
**File**: `extensions-terraform/about/src/lib.rs:38-55`

**What**: `AboutTerraformExtension` and the `Extension` impl generated by `ops_extension::impl_extension!` are the crate's entire public surface, and nothing in the test module touches them. The 18 tests cover `TerraformIdentityProvider` (a private type) and the private parse helpers; `provider_name` (`:436-440`) asserts the provider's own `name()` string, not that the extension registers under it.

Untested as a result: `name` / `description` / `shortname`, `types() == ExtensionType::DATASOURCE`, `stack() == Some(Stack::Terraform)`, `data_provider_name() == Some("project_identity")`, and — the one with real wiring risk — `register_data_providers` actually inserting `TerraformIdentityProvider` into a `DataRegistry` under `DATA_PROVIDER_NAME`.

**Why it matters**: These constants are the contract between this crate and the extension host; a typo or a drift between `DATA_PROVIDER_NAME` and the registration key produces an extension that compiles, links into the `linkme` registry, and silently provides nothing — the About card falls back with no error. Every parse-level test in this file would still pass. One test that builds a `DataRegistry`, calls `register_data_providers`, and looks the provider up would close the whole class.

**Note**: no sibling about crate tests its extension impl either, so a shared assertion helper in `ops_about::test_support` (which this crate already has as a dev-dependency via `ops-extension`'s `test-support` feature) would let all six adopt it; this task is scoped to this crate.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- AC:BEGIN -->
- [x] #1 A test asserts the Extension metadata: name, shortname, types, stack and data_provider_name
- [x] #2 A test asserts that register_data_providers registers a provider under "project_identity" in a DataRegistry
- [x] #3 cargo test -p ops-about-terraform passes
